about.title: Farmersville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Farmersville households rely on farm equipment, vehicles, tools, and household products every day, and most of the time they work fine. But when a product fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the results can be serious injuries that disrupt work and family life across Tulare County. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim against manufacturers, distributors, or retailers without having to prove negligence — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That's an important distinction for Farmersville residents dealing with medical bills after using a product exactly as intended. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your family, holding onto the item, its packaging, and any manuals can matter later. Our team handles product liability claims and can review what happened and explain your options, with no upfront cost since we work on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make a real difference for Farmersville residents facing an uphill fight against a large manufacturer.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. We can help identify which parties were involved in getting the product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, packaging, and instructions intact after an injury can be critical evidence. Our team can advise you on how to preserve what you have before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows product liability claims under strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the company was careless. We can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try not to throw it away, repair it, or return it to the store. Store it safely along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts, since the item itself is often the most important piece of evidence in a defect claim.
